appraisal_events.evidence: « Jamais le public n'a fait preuve d'un calme aussi admirable. » (M. de Norpois aurait bien voulu que ce fût vrai, mais craignait tout le contraire.)
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator's parenthetical aside punctures the confident public rhetoric of the article Norpois has sent, revealing that he privately fears the opposite of what he asserts, exposing a gap between his polished diplomatic prose and his real anxiety.

appraisal_events.evidence: je n'avais pas de joie qu'elle fût vivante, que je ne l'aimais plus... le souvenir qui me vint fut celui d'une fille fort grosse, hommasse, dans le visage fané de laquelle saillait déjà, comme une graine, le profil de Mme Bontemps... J'avais définitivement cessé d'aimer Albertine.
appraisal_events.explanation: Although a telegram reveals Albertine is alive, the narrator's love has already been dissolved by forgetting; her remembered image degrades into an unflattering, aged figure, and the passage explicitly denies any revival of feeling, marking her definitive diminishment in his emotional life.

status_effects.explanation: Norpois is locally deflated by the narrator's revelation that his confident public text masks private fear, undercutting the authority of his own rhetoric.
Albertine's remembered image is reduced from a radiant girl to an unflattering, coarse, aged figure resembling Mme Bontemps.
The narrator explicitly and definitively stops loving Albertine, and the news of her survival fails to restore any emotional hold she once had over him.
